slides.heading: Remove Islands
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Remove Islands, a medium graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Set to 0 every group of 1s not connected (4-directionally) to the matrix border.
Flood-fill from border 1s marking them, then clear the rest.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Set to 0 every group of 1s not connected (4-directionally) to the matrix border. Flood-fill from border 1s marking them, then clear the rest.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Ones connected to the border survive; everything else is an island to remove.
slides.narration: Ones connected to the border survive; everything else is an island to remove.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: DFS from each interior 1 to see if it reaches the border → O((w·h)²)
Flip the question: flood-fill from the border → O(w·h)
Mark safe cells in place (2), then rewrite
slides.narration: Checking each interior one separately for a path to the border repeats work. Flipping the question, flood-filling from the border to mark safe cells, solves it in one linear pass.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Flood-fill from every border one, marking them safe
2. Turn the remaining ones into zeros
slides.narration: Step by step. First, flood-fill from every border one, marking them safe. Second, turn the remaining ones into zeros. Third, restore the safe marks.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Border 1s are safe (not islands)
slides.narration: Any one on the border, and anything connected to it, isn't an island. Start a flood fill from every border one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Flood fill done: red cells are islands
slides.narration: After the flood fill, the green ones are connected to the border. The red ones are islands.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Islands removed
slides.narration: Turn the islands into zeros. Everything connected to the border stays.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We push every border one onto a stack and mark it two. Popping cells, we mark and push neighbouring ones. Finally, cells marked two become one and everything else becomes zero.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of w times h. Space is O of w times h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Recursive DFS can overflow on large grids → use a stack
slides.narration: Only four directions count. Use an explicit stack to avoid recursion depth problems, and convert the temporary marks back at the end.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: This is the surrounded regions pattern; counting islands is the River Sizes problem.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Ones connected to the border survive; everything else is an island to remove.
slides.narration: To recap Remove Islands: Ones connected to the border survive; everything else is an island to remove. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
